speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether he can provide more details on the digital vaccine passport system between Singapore and Australia and travel bubble arrangements with countries that have the COVID-19 pandemic under control.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, vaccinations are only one aspect of pandemic control.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Social distancing, contact tracing, quarantine and testing are also very important aspects which countries and regions have used to control the spread of the COVID-19 virus even as vaccines become available.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And we have been proactively doing so, given the importance of our global connections.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for the comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: One, how would the recent announcement by the Hong Kong government to bar Singapore Airlines (SIA) from flying to Hong Kong for two weeks, affect the negotiation or the preparation of the travel bubble between Hong Kong and Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And two, will the Minister reveal which are the countries we are negotiating with and preparing for travel bubble over the next few months?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hong Kong's civil aviation authorities set in place very transparent criteria for airlines.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Once they breach the criteria, they get suspended for 14 days.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, they have suspended 23 times before this latest incident, involving SIA.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The suspension came about because of technical reasons.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One of the criteria was breached, which is that SIA had a transit passenger, not from Singapore, tested negative at pre-departure, but tested positive at post-arrival.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, maybe an old case with intermittent shedding.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And at the same time, I believe there were a few passengers who tested negative but carrying certificates from labs that are not ISO-certified.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Hong Kong civil aviation authorities enforce the criteria very strictly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for how many countries we are speaking to, there are many.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I actually do not quite like the term "vaccination passports".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It gives you the impression like we carry a passport and we can go anywhere.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think what happens is every healthcare authority, after vaccination, issues a vaccination certificate that has to be verifiable, tamper-proof.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And then, we talk to other regions and authorities to mutually recognise our certificates.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is the part where we are talking to many partners because it is good to mutually recognise our certificates.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And after you mutually recognise the certificates, then you ask yourself, "So what?" Are you therefore – which is a question that Ms Foo Mee Har asked – subject to shorter quarantine, fewer tests?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are things that we have to discuss.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the first criterion in such discussions would be, how safe is this region?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, that is the first and foremost criterion.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And if it is moderately safe, then we can consider relaxing restrictions for vaccinated travellers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: From time to time, you will see public statements being made, but actually behind the scenes, a lot of work is going on.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When there are significant progress and significant things to announce, we will do so and inform the public.
